meanings.usage: 通常搭配介词for，表示对某事物的强烈喜爱

meanings.meaning: 以…为借口，抗辩（后接名词作宾语，常见搭配plead ignorance（声称不知情））

meanings.usage: 修饰动词，描述人做某事时愉快的状态
常搭配介词on/upon，指开始一项新的或重要的活动
搭配介词for，表示满足某人或某群体的需求
指在某一领域没有经验的人
常搭配介词for，表示释放某种情绪或能量的渠道
用来形容人善于应对各种困难
常搭配live under the delusion that，表示抱有错误的想法
指把机器、结构等拆成多个部件

meanings.meaning: verb（过去分词）. 断裂，绷断
meanings.usage: 常用来描述细线、链条等硬物突然折断

meanings.meaning: 难以克服的，无法解决的
meanings.usage: 常修饰问题、困难等，表示难度极大无法应对

meanings.meaning: 拼图游戏，错综复杂的事物
meanings.usage: jigsaw puzzle指拼图，也可比喻复杂难理清的情况
通常指反复抱怨或催促某人做某事

meanings.meaning: handyman；n.   手巧的人，能工巧匠
fuse；v.   由于烧断保险丝而短路

phrases.usage: 抽出时间做（一直想做的事）

examples.en: I've been meaning to fix the shelf, but I never got round to it.
examples.zh: 我一直想修那个架子，但始终抽不出时间做。

examples.en: They spent three months laying out their new garden.
examples.zh: 他们花了三个月布置新花园。

examples.en: Some fans go so far as to wait outside the hotel for hours just to see the star.
examples.zh: 一些粉丝甚至在酒店外等好几个小时，就为了看明星一眼。

examples.en: This restaurant caters for vegetarians with a special menu.
examples.zh: 这家餐厅有专门的菜单满足素食者的需求。

examples.en: He lives under the delusion that he can win the game without practice.
examples.zh: 他误以为不用练习就能赢得比赛。

phrases.usage: 请来，叫（专业人士）来帮忙

examples.en: We had to call in a plumber to fix the blocked pipe.
examples.zh: 我们不得不请水管工来修堵塞的管道。

examples.en: My mother would not hear of me walking home alone at night.
examples.zh: 我妈妈不同意我晚上独自走路回家。

examples.en: The floor was littered with toy bricks after the kids played.
examples.zh: 孩子们玩过之后，地板上散落着积木。

examples.en: Needless to say, the concert was canceled because of the bad weather.
examples.zh: 不用说，演唱会因为恶劣天气取消了。

grammar.title: so...that...引导的倒装句
grammar.structure: So + adj./adv. + be动词/助动词/情态动词 + 主语 + that + 结果状语从句
grammar.definition: 当so+形容词/副词位于句首表示强调时，句子需要部分倒装，用来加强语气 用于强调形容词或副词所描述的程度，引出后面的结果

examples.en: So great is our passion for doing things for ourselves, that we are becoming increasingly less dependent on specialized labour.
examples.zh: 我们自己动手的热情是如此高涨，以至于我们越来越不依赖专业劳动力。

examples.en: So fast did he run that no one could catch up with him.
examples.zh: 他跑得太快了，没人能追上他。

grammar.title: 虚拟语气在suggest后的宾语从句中的用法
grammar.structure: 主语 + suggest + that + 主语 + (should) + 动词原形 + 其他
grammar.definition: 当suggest表示“建议”时，后面的宾语从句需要用虚拟语气，即谓语动词为should+动词原形，should可以省略 用于表达建议、要求、命令等含义的动词后的宾语从句中

examples.en: Last spring my wife suggested that I call in a man to look at our lawn mower.
examples.zh: 去年春天，我妻子建议我请个人来看看我们的割草机。

examples.en: The teacher suggested that we (should) finish the project before Friday.
examples.zh: 老师建议我们在周五之前完成这个项目。

original.en: Some really keen enthusiasts go so far as to build their own computers.
original.zh: 一些真正热衷的人甚至自己组装电脑。

imitations.en: Some pet owners go so far as to buy expensive clothes for their cats.
imitations.zh: 一些宠物主人甚至给他们的猫买昂贵的衣服。

imitations.en: Some students go so far as to stay up all night to prepare for the exam.
imitations.zh: 一些学生甚至通宵复习准备考试。

original.en: The worst thing about the do-it-yourself game is that sometimes even men live under the delusion that they can do anything.
original.zh: 自己动手最糟糕的一点是，有时候就连男人们也会误以为自己什么都能做。

imitations.en: The worst thing about travelling alone is that you have no one to share the beautiful scenery with.
imitations.zh: 独自旅行最糟糕的一点是，你没有人可以分享美丽的风景。

imitations.en: The worst thing about forgetting your phone is that you can't contact anyone when you need help.
imitations.zh: 忘带手机最糟糕的一点是，你需要帮助的时候联系不上任何人。

patterns.pattern: As far as I could see, it needed only...

original.en: As far as I could see, it needed only a minor adjustment: a turn of a screw here, a little tightening up there, a drop of oil and it would be as good as new.
original.zh: 在我看来，它只需要一点小小的调整：这里拧一下螺丝，那里紧一紧，滴点油，就会跟新的一样了。

imitations.en: As far as I could see, the cake needed only a little more cream on top to be perfect.
imitations.zh: 在我看来，这个蛋糕只需要在顶部多加一点奶油就完美了。

imitations.en: As far as I could see, the plan needed only a few small changes to be workable.
imitations.zh: 在我看来，这个计划只需要几处小改动就可行了。

patterns.pattern: When..., I told her that either...or...

original.en: When my wife nagged me to do something about it, I told her that either I would have to buy a new mower or let the grass grow.
original.zh: 当我妻子催我想想办法的时候，我告诉她要么我买个新的割草机，要么就让草继续长。

imitations.en: When my friend asked where to have dinner, I told her that either we can eat at the new restaurant nearby or order takeout.
imitations.zh: 当我朋友问去哪里吃晚饭的时候，我告诉她要么我们去附近的新餐厅吃，要么点外卖。

imitations.en: When the teacher asked about our weekend plan, I said that either we would visit the museum or go hiking.
imitations.zh: 当老师问起我们的周末计划时，我说我们要么去参观博物馆，要么去远足。

translation:
现在我们自己动手做事的热情很高，结果对于专业工人的依赖越来越少了。由于出版了不计其数的教人自己动手做事的书报杂志，没有人再能说对某事一无所知。新婚夫妇找来合适的工具和材料，喜气洋洋地开始布置新房。特别是男人，常利用空闲时间安装壁炉、布置花园、建造车库、制作家具。有些热衷于自己动手的人甚至自己组装电脑。为了满足自己动手热的需要，商店不仅为初学者提供专门的咨询服务，而且为顾客准备了各种零件，供他们买回家去安装。这些东西为人们潜在的创造力提供了一个绝妙的用武之地。但不幸的是，我们并非人人都是能工巧匠。
妻子常常认为她们的丈夫无比聪明能干。甚至那些连一枚钉子都钉不直的男人都被认为是天生的电工、木匠、水管工和机械师。每当电灯保险丝烧断、家具榫头松动、管道堵塞、吸尘器不动时，有些妻子认为丈夫总有办法。自己动手的例子中最糟糕的是，有时甚至是男人尽管接连失败却还误以为自己什么都行，原因就是要面子。
今年春天，妻子让我请人检查一下我家的割草机。那台割草机去年夏天就坏了，尽管我答应修，但一直没抽出时间，我不愿听妻子的建议，说我自己会修。一个星期六的下午，我把割草机拉到了花园里，仔细检查了一番。在我看来，只需稍加调整即可。这儿紧紧螺丝，那儿固定一下，再加几滴油，就会像新的一样了。事实上，修理工作远不是那么简单。修完后割草机还是纹丝不动。于是，我决定把它拆开。一会儿工夫，割草机便被拆成一个个金属零件，乱七八糟地堆在花园里。但我却非常高兴，因为我找到了毛病所在。驱动轮子的链条断了一节。我买来一根新链条后，面临的就是如何把这些令人眼花缭乱的拼板重新组装起来。等我装完后，那台割草机仍然一动不动，对此我倒并不感到吃惊。原因很简单，因为还剩下几个形状奇特的零件似乎哪里也装不上去。我无可奈何，只好罢休。几个星期过去了，草长了起来。妻子喋喋不休让我想点办法。我告诉她，要么买一台新割草机，要么让草长下去。不用说，我家现在已被丛林包围。深草丛中的某个地方有一台正在生锈的割草机，那就是我曾答应某日要修理的割草机。

text.title: Do it yourself     自己动手

lines.en: So great is our passion for doing things for ourselves, that we are becoming increasingly less dependent on specialized labour.
No one can plead ignorance of a subject any longer, for these are countless do-it-yourself publications.
Armed with the right tools and materials, newlyweds gaily embark on the task of decorating their own homes.
Men, particularly, spend hours of their leisure time installing their own fireplaces, laying out their own gardens; building garages and making furniture.
Some really keen enthusiasts go so far as to build their own computers.
Shops cater for the do-it-yourself craze not only by running special advisory services for novices , but by offering consumers bits and pieces which they can assemble at home.
Such things provide an excellent outlet for pent up creative energy, but unfortunately not all of us are born handymen.
Some wives tend to believe that their husbands are infinitely resourceful and can fix anything.
Even men who can hardly drive a nail in straight are supposed to be born electricians, carpenters, plumbers and mechanics.
When lights fuse, furniture gets rickety, pipes get clogged , or vacuum cleaners fail to operate, some woman assume that their husbands will somehow put things right.
The worst thing about the do-it-yourself game is that sometimes even men live under the delusion that they can do anything, even when they have repeatedly been proved wrong.
It is a question of pride as much as anything else.
Last spring my wife suggested that I call in a man to look at our lawn mower.
It had broken down the previous summer, and though I promised to repair it, I had never got round to it.
I would not hear of the suggestion and said that I would fix it myself.
One Saturday afternoon, I hauled the machine into the garden and had a close look at it.
As far as I could see, it needed only a minor adjustment: a turn of a screw here, a little tightening up there, a drop of oil and it would be as good as new.
Inevitably the repair job was not quite so simple.
The mower firmly refused to mow , so I decided to dismantle it.
The garden was soon littered with chunks of metal which had once made up a lawn mower.
But I was extremely pleased with myself.
I had traced the cause of the trouble.
One of links in the chain that drives the wheels had snapped.
After buying a new chain I was faced with the insurmountable task of putting the confusing jigsaw puzzle together again.

I was not surprised to find that the machine still refused to work after I had reassembled it, for the simple reason that I was left with several curiously shaped bits of metal which did not seem to fit anywhere.
I gave up in despair.
The weeks passed and the grass grew.
When my wife nagged me to do something about it, I told her that either I would have to buy a new mower or let the grass grow.
Needless to say our house is now surrounded by a jungle.
Buried somewhere in deep grass there is a rusting lawn mower which I have promised to repair one day.

lead.summary: 《自己动手》现在我们自己动手做事的热情很高，结果对于专业工人的依赖越来越少了。由于出版了不计其数的教人自己动手做事的书报杂志，没有人再能说对某事一无所知。语法聚焦：on top of, 在……上面。。
lead.tips: 语法重点：on top of, 在……上面。。重点词汇：plead、ignorance、publication 等，结合课文例句记忆。练法：先盲听跟读，再对照参考译文理解，最后尝试复述课文。
lead.question: Did the writer repair his lawn mower in the end? Why/Why not?
